layers.text: When your monthly salary arrives in your hands,
or when you set a value for your labor,
there is a quiet voice of doubt inside you.
With a subtle feeling that whispers "I do not deserve this",
how many opportunities have you passed up?
what secretly controls our opportunities and expenses
is not just a lack of money, but
what if it is the hidden belief we carry about ourselves?
This situation is deeply familiar to many of us.
How you should manage your money,
you know well that you should save or make a budget.
Yet, at the exact moment of decision,
an invisible doubt pulls you back.
When you think about asking for a salary raise,
or when asking for the true value your work deserves,
the voice inside you says, "You are not there yet."
And because of this wall of doubt,
we often stay away from long-term financial plans;
and instead of moving toward saving,
we are drawn toward emergency loans.

Simply knowing how to manage your money
is not enough on its own to take action.
When 64 scientific studies across 24 years were synthesized,
people who believe in their ability—more than those with equal income—
were proven to successfully manage savings and expense budgets.
Does this belief really change people income?
To answer this question, a 7-year study was conducted in Germany.
from the very start of their careers.
When their belief in their professional capability was measured at entry,
3 and 7 years later, those with high capability beliefs—
even with identical academic performance and profession—
achieved significantly higher salaries and career growth.
Why does this belief create such a large difference in income?
Because when you believe in your capability,
you do not easily give up in the face of workplace obstacles.
It helps you ask for the true value of your work,
However, we must understand one crucial and fundamental truth.
Changing your mindset alone will not magically make you rich;
nor is poverty caused by a bad mindset.
journal, a published study proved that
financial hardship causes so much mental stress
that it weakens our thinking just like staying awake all night—
reducing our cognitive capacity (IQ) by about 13 points.
Because financial strain puts our minds under severe pressure,
the hidden belief you hold about yourself
will not magically change your bank account tomorrow.
your perspective on your capability quietly guides the small decisions you make today.
And it is these hidden decisions
that quietly write your future financial story.
So how do we break this invisible wall between our mind and reality?
We will explore the scientifically proven solution in our next episode...
